items.title: @astrojs/vercel: `middlewareMode: 'edge'` is silently inert when `isr` is enabled

labels.name: - P3: minor bug
labels.description: An edge case that only affects very specific usage (priority)

labels.name: triage: unable to reproduce
labels.description: Triage bot attempted reproduction but could not reproduce

items.body:
### Astro Info

```block
Astro                    v7.2.2
Node                     v24.18.1
System                   Linux (x64)
Package Manager          pnpm
Output                   server
Adapter                  @astrojs/vercel v11.0.5
Integrations             none
```

### If this issue only occurs in one browser, which browser is a problem?

_No response_

### Describe the Bug

With `@astrojs/vercel`, setting both `middlewareMode: 'edge'` and `isr` produces a
`_middleware` edge function that is built, bundled and deployed, but that no page
route ever invokes. The option silently does nothing.

In `packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts`, the non-ISR branch points every
on-demand route at the middleware (`dest = _middlewareEntryPoint ? MIDDLEWARE_PATH : NODE_PATH`).
The ISR branch points them at the ISR function instead, so `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` survives
only for `isr.exclude` entries and the 404 catch-all. `buildMiddlewareFolder()` is then
called regardless, so the edge function is produced and uploaded either way.

Generated `.vercel/output/config.json` for a fixture with `middlewareMode: 'edge'` plus
`isr: { expiration: 120 }` and nothing else:

```json
{ "src": "^/$",      "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=…" },
{ "src": "^/404/?$", "dest": "/_isr?x_astro_path=$0&x_astro_path_token=…" },
{ "src": "^/.*$",    "dest": "_middleware", "status": 404 }
```

The only route pointing at `_middleware` is the 404 catch-all.

The runtime consequence is that middleware only runs inside the ISR function — Vercel's
ISR caches on the path and, on a cache hit, does not invoke the function at all. So any
middleware on an ISR-enabled Vercel site stops running once an entry is warm: security
headers, redirects, auth gates, geo, A/B, content negotiation. Running ahead of the cache
is the reason edge middleware exists, and the one configuration where it is needed is the
one where the routing to it is dropped.

Observed on a live site (`output: 'server'`, `isr: { expiration: 86400 }`,
`edgeMiddleware: true`) that negotiates HTML vs. Markdown on `/` from the `Accept`
header:

```console
$ curl -sI -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://<site>/
content-type: text/html          # should be text/markdown
x-vercel-cache: HIT              # the middleware never ran
age: 535
```

Its build output contained a 1.9 MB `_middleware.func` reachable from nothing but 404s.

### What's the expected result?


Either of:

1. **Minimum:** the adapter warns (or throws) at build time when `isr` and
   `middlewareMode: 'edge'` are both set, instead of shipping a function nothing calls.
2. **Preferred:** on-demand routes are pointed at `MIDDLEWARE_PATH` in the ISR branch too, and
   the generated middleware's `next()` forwards to `/_isr?x_astro_path=…&x_astro_path_token=…`
   for ISR-backed routes and `/_render` for routes matched by `isr.exclude`, so cached
   responses are still served while the middleware runs first.

(2) is what PR #17687 implements, with a fixture and route-table assertions. Note the tradeoff
stated there: every request to an ISR route then invokes the edge function, including cache
hits. That is inherent to asking for edge middleware, applies only when
`middlewareMode: 'edge'` is set, and the alternative today is middleware that silently does
not run.

Vercel's native `x-middleware-next` protocol is not a usable alternative here: Astro's `next()`
must return a `Response` so middleware can post-process it, and `x-middleware-next` only hands
off. That is why the adapter generates a full handler that `fetch`es `/_render`.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://github.com/asmyshlyaev177/astro-isr-middleware-repro

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

items.title: buildCacheControlDirectives() never returns undefined when extraDirectives are passed, so uncached routes are announced as cacheable

labels.name: - P4: important
labels.description: Violate documented behavior or significantly impacts performance (priority)

labels.name: triage: fix pending

items.body:
### Astro Info

```
astro                    v7.3.1
@astrojs/cloudflare      v14.3.0
```

Also present on `main` as of today — `packages/astro/src/core/cache/provider-utils.ts` and all three first-party cache providers are unchanged.

### Describe the Bug

`buildCacheControlDirectives()` documents itself as "Returns `undefined` if no caching directives are present". It does not, whenever a provider passes `extraDirectives` — which all three first-party providers do unconditionally.

```ts
export function buildCacheControlDirectives(
	options: CacheOptions,
	extraDirectives?: string[],
): string | undefined {
	const directives: string[] = [];

	if (extraDirectives) {
		directives.push(...extraDirectives);   // <-- pushed before maxAge/swr are examined
	}

	if (options.maxAge !== undefined) { directives.push(`max-age=${options.maxAge}`); }
	if (options.swr !== undefined) { directives.push(`stale-while-revalidate=${options.swr}`); }

	return directives.length > 0 ? directives.join(', ') : undefined;
}
```

`directives` is never empty once extras are pushed, so the return is never `undefined`.

Every provider guards on that return value:

- `packages/integrations/cloudflare/src/cache/provider.ts` — `buildCacheControlDirectives(options, ['public'])`, then `if (directives) headers.set('Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control', directives)`
- `packages/integrations/netlify/src/cache/provider.ts` — `['public', 'durable']`
- `packages/integrations/vercel/src/cache/provider.ts` — `['public']`

The guard is always true. So a route with **no** `maxAge` and **no** `swr` still emits `<Platform>-CDN-Cache-Control: public`, telling the CDN the response is cacheable.

This is reachable in normal use because `AstroCache[APPLY_HEADERS]` skips the provider only when `maxAge` is undefined **and** there are no tags:

```js
if (finalOptions.maxAge === undefined && !finalOptions.tags?.length) return;
```

A CMS loader's `cacheHint` typically carries tags and no `maxAge`. So `Astro.cache.set(cacheHint)` on a route with no `routeRules` entry reaches `setHeaders()` and gets announced as cacheable.

On Cloudflare there is a second consequence. `applyCloudflareResponseHeaders` (`packages/integrations/cloudflare/src/utils/response.ts`) sets `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: no-store` only on a response that does not already carry that header:

```ts
const needsNoStoreDefault = cacheProviderEnabled && !response.headers.has('Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control');
```

Because the provider always sets the header, that safety default never fires.

### What's the expected result?

A route with no `maxAge` and no `swr` should not be announced to the CDN as cacheable. `buildCacheControlDirectives` should behave as documented and return `undefined` when there are no real caching directives, so each provider's `if (directives)` guard works and — on Cloudflare — the adapter's `no-store` default can still fire.

### Observed impact

On a real Astro 7.3.1 site on Cloudflare Workers (`@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.3.0, `cache: { provider: cacheCloudflare() }`, `"cache": { "enabled": true }`), deployed to an environment whose `routeRules` is `{}` and which should therefore cache nothing:

| Route | `cf-cache-status` |
| --- | --- |
| `/`, `/posts`, `/posts/[slug]` | `MISS`, then `HIT` with a climbing `age` |
| `/search?q=…` | `MISS`, then `HIT` with a climbing `age` |
| `/notify/confirm?token=…` | `MISS`, then `EXPIRED` |
| `/ip` | `BYPASS` |

Every cached route calls `Astro.cache.set(cacheHint)`. `/ip` is the only one that does not — it is an `APIRoute` that never calls it, so nothing set the header, so the adapter's `no-store` default fired and Cloudflare bypassed it. That contrast is what isolated the cause.

Caching per-query search results and token-bearing confirmation pages is a correctness and privacy problem, not just a performance one.

Four things that do **not** work as an opt-out, in case they come up:

- Removing `"cache": { "enabled": true }` from `wrangler.jsonc` — the adapter re-injects it into the generated `dist/server/wrangler.json` whenever `cache.enabled` is `undefined`. Only an explicit `false` disables it.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` from user middleware — lower precedence than `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` at the edge.
- `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: no-store` from user middleware, or deleting `Cache-Tag` there — both overwritten, since `handleCache()` wraps `handleMiddleware()` and the provider's headers are applied after middleware returns.

`Astro.cache.set(false)` does work per-route, since it returns before the provider is consulted. `Astro.cache.set({ maxAge: 0 })` does not — it yields `public, max-age=0`, which still carries `Last-Modified`/`ETag` for revalidation.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

No deployment needed — the core function can be called directly:

```js
import { buildCacheControlDirectives } from 'astro/dist/core/cache/provider-utils.js';

console.log(buildCacheControlDirectives({}, ['public']));                 // "public"      — expected undefined
console.log(buildCacheControlDirectives({ tags: ['posts'] }, ['public'])); // "public"      — expected undefined
console.log(buildCacheControlDirectives({}, undefined));                  // undefined     — correct
console.log(buildCacheControlDirectives({ maxAge: 300 }, ['public']));    // "public, max-age=300" — correct
```

The second line is the case that reaches production: a loader `cacheHint` with tags and no `maxAge`.

### Suggested fix

Compute the real directives first and prepend `extraDirectives` only if that produced something:

```ts
const directives: string[] = [];

if (options.maxAge !== undefined) directives.push(`max-age=${options.maxAge}`);
if (options.swr !== undefined) directives.push(`stale-while-revalidate=${options.swr}`);

if (directives.length === 0) return undefined;
return [...(extraDirectives ?? []), ...directives].join(', ');
```

Worth considering alongside it: the providers set `Cache-Tag` unconditionally even when there are no directives and no tags, where core's own `defaultSetHeaders` gates it on `tags.length`.

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.
